It uses L-BFGS-B with analytic gradients on a fixed multi-resolution ladder (64→4096 knots) with hand-tuned time shares, instead of the record's approach. It initializes from random Gaussian packets and upsamples by i…

This program optimizes a Dinkelbach-style surrogate (smooth-max minus λ·num) with L-BFGS-B gradients on a fixed grid, rather than the record's approach of building a tuned small-n construction and carefully upsampling it. It grows resolution by repeat-upsampling through a fixed stage ladder (64→2048) with per-stage time shares, whereas the record avoided interpolation because it destroys tuned st…

This program starts from the given `start` and refines it with local, parameterised moves (run scaling, additive cosine packets, constant-run shifts, bump replacement, and pairwise mass transfer), each tuned by a 1-D grid-plus-golden-section line search along the projected ray, rather than building a fresh tuned construction. It keeps the L2 normalisation fixed and optimises the exact piecewise-q…

This program uses linear interpolation to upsample between fixed ladder sizes (256→4096) rather than repeat-based upsampling, and it anneals the smooth-max exponent p from 4 to 400 within each stage instead of re-annealing a beta parameter from a warm start. It also allocates time across stages by increasing weights and runs a final high-p polish loop, whereas the record's program concentrated it…

This program builds a hand-crafted spike-plus-decaying-comb seed at n=512 and then doubles resolution in four stages (512→1024→2048→4096), spending only 20% of budget on the first stage and re-annealing beta from 1e4 upward at each new resolution, whereas the record reuses its existing 16384 resolution and puts the whole budget into polishing at max n. This program builds a hand-crafted seed of a 10-tooth raised-cosine comb plus a graded ramp of 30 bumps, then grows it by coordinate-wise golden-section tuning of per-run multiplicative factors and additive bumps (doubling resolution only when stuck), whereas the record relies on a tuned small-n construction polished by Dinkelbach LSE gradient ascent at fixed high resolution. It optimises a smoothed piecewise-quadratic surrogate of ||f*f||_2^2 (trapezoid-style averaging of adjacent convolution values…

This program abandons the record's multi-resolution pipeline (refine at 4096/8192/32768 then pool down) and instead works directly at a single fixed resolution (N=1024), starting from the constant-ones seed rather than a tuned construction.
